title: Multiancestry genome-wide association and multiomics analyses elucidate spatiocellular features of multiple sclerosis genetics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: NBDC (Japan's National Bioscience Database Center) dataset NHA000209 page: unrestricted access, 1.2 GB. Fetched the readme (column dictionary). HEAD on the zip: 1,156,348,648 bytes. Ranged reads of the zip's file index list 4 gzipped TSVs (GWAS, genome-wide association study, summary statistics on hg19): African 272 MB, cross-population 429 MB, European 208 MB, Japanese 247 MB. Decoded the first ~14,000 rows of the African file: columns CHR, POS, SNP, EA, NEA, P, BETA, SE, OR, Z, Direction, parsing cleanly. Also saw that single-cell data E-GEAD-1251 (PBMCs, peripheral blood immune cells, from 20 MS patients) is listed as unrestricted, and that the raw single-cell data JGAD001005 is controlled access.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Case and control counts (29,374 cases, 1,843,563 controls), the 22 novel loci, and the cell-type enrichment results. Total variant counts per file were not seen, because the full files exceed the 50 MB cap. Individual-level genotypes (UK Biobank, All of Us, Genomics England, MVP through dbGaP) need access applications. The lesion snRNA-seq and spatial data come from a different study's UCSC Cell Browser.

a1_downloadable.note: Summary statistics are unrestricted on NBDC NHA000209 and the zip responds to a direct download (checked). Individual-level genotypes are controlled access, but the project doesn't need them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Each variant does have BETA/Z columns (checked), but these are association statistics smeared across correlated nearby variants (LD, linkage disequilibrium), not one measured outcome per item. A usable label such as 'causal variant' or 'causal gene' would have to be built by fine-mapping, a statistical method that picks the likely causal variant at each locus.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genomic coordinates and alleles are present (hg19), so sequence context could be pulled from the reference genome.

a4_units_stated.note: The readme states BETA is a log odds ratio, gives SE (standard error), OR (odds ratio), Z and P, and says positions are on hg19.

a5_enough_rows.note: Probably millions of variants per file (the gz files are 208–429 MB), but the total wasn't counted. At the locus level there are only about 200+ independent loci, which is tiny.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.16 GB compressed; one ancestry file is 208–429 MB gz
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits on the laptop if streamed with pandas in chunks.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The NBDC page's cohort counts match the abstract (29,374 cases and 1,843,563 controls cross-population). Variant counts were not verified.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any per-variant 'causal' label would come from a fine-mapping model (SuSiE or PolyFun posteriors), so the project would be distilling another model. Predicting raw Z-scores from annotations is a heritability-enrichment analysis, which the paper itself already does.

existing_models.name: PolyFun + SuSiE (functionally informed fine-mapping, Weissbrod et al. 2020, Nature Genetics)
existing_models.score_and_split: >32% more fine-mapped variants (posterior causal probability above 0.95) than SuSiE alone across 49 UK Biobank traits; evaluated in simulations and on UK Biobank data.

existing_models.name: V2D variant-to-disease machine-learning framework (PMC12633601)
existing_models.score_and_split: Models disease effect sizes from fine-mapping posteriors plus ~100 functional annotations; scores not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Borzoi-informed fine mapping (bioRxiv 2025.07.09.663936)
existing_models.score_and_split: Uses a deep-learning DNA sequence model as a fine-mapping prior; scores not retrieved.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Borzoi variant-effect scores as features (the DNA models are not fine-tuned)

integration.partner_dataset: GWAS Catalog / FinnGen summary statistics; AlphaGenome precomputed variant effects
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the Japanese-specific MS risk variants have regulatory effects in immune cells that European-trained priors miss? This is a fine-mapping question, not a supervised one.

controls.positive_control: The HLA-DRB1*15:01 signal in the MHC (major histocompatibility complex) region
controls.external_validation: IMSGC (International MS Genetics Consortium) European fine-mapping

honest_claim_h3: At best, the model ranks variants by prior causal probability at MS loci, judged against fine-mapping posteriors that are themselves model outputs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence and regulatory annotations around each genetic variant to predict whether it truly drives multiple sclerosis risk.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-variant DNA context and functional annotations for the variants in the four ancestry summary-statistic files. The variant total is unknown (the files weren't fully downloaded).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a variant is causal at a risk locus. No measured truth exists: it would come from statistical fine-mapping of association signals, which is another model's output.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Statistical geneticists would get better candidate variants for experimental follow-up in non-European populations. But this task is already served by open fine-mapping tools.

ml_idea: Rejected. The only supervised framing is 'predict causal variant from annotations', and its label is a fine-mapping posterior (circular) or an LD-smeared association statistic. That framing is functionally informed fine-mapping, which PolyFun and similar tools already cover openly.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project was rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent genome-wide significant loci (about 200+), which is the real unit of supervision. It is far below the 400 needed.

verdict_reason: The data downloads freely and parses cleanly (NBDC NHA000209, 4 TSVs, checked). But these are GWAS summary statistics: there is no measured per-item label, and any 'causal variant' label would be a fine-mapping model output (A2 and A8 fail). The single-cell part has only 20 patients.
